The proposed solution is incorrect. 

In coding theory, the **Schur square** (or Hadamard square / componentwise product square) of a code $C \subseteq F^n$ is defined as 
$$C^{\star 2} = C \star C = \operatorname{span}\{u \star v \mid u, v \in C\},$$
where $\star$ denotes the componentwise product. Because the componentwise product is commutative ($u \star v = v \star u$), the dimension of the Schur square of a code of dimension $t$ cannot exceed $\binom{t+1}{2} = \frac{t(t+1)}{2} < t^2$ (for $t \ge 2$). The proposed solution confuses the Schur square with the full tensor product space $C \otimes C$.

VERDICT: REJECT
